title: Mastering Corneal Graft Redo: Surgical Strategies & Management
summary: Corneal graft redo procedures represent a high-stakes challenge in anterior segment surgery, often necessitated by endothelial failure or immunologic rejection. This guide navigates the complexities of secondary keratoplasty, from risk stratification to advanced surgical decision-making.

sections.title: Risk Stratification: The Collaborative Corneal Transplantation Studies (CCTS)
Red Flags for Impending Failure
content: Acute rise in IOP (steroid-induced or synechial)

content.explanation: Keratic precipitates, Hazy cornea (edema), Overlying epithelial line (Khodadoust), Decreased vision, Anterior chamber cells/flare.

sections.title: Pre-operative Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 2: AS-OCT to evaluate retrocorneal membranes and iris-cornea adhesion.
Step 3: Specular microscopy on the donor button (if feasible) to assess endothelial reserve.
Step 4: B-Scan Ultrasound to rule out posterior segment pathology (retinal detachment, endophthalmitis).
Step 5: Infectious workup (culture/PCR) if etiology of primary failure is suspected to be microbial.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Systemic immunosuppression (e.g., Mycophenolate Mofetil 1g BID) is mandatory for patients with >2 prior graft failures.
Always perform a thorough gonioscopy to identify hidden peripheral anterior synechiae that contribute to secondary glaucoma.
For high-risk eyes, consider the use of prophylactic anti-VEGF (Bevacizumab) subconjunctival injections to regress neovascularization prior to surgery.
Post-op steroid tapering in redo cases must be significantly slower than in primary grafts, often spanning 6-12 months.
Monitor for 'Stellate Endotheliopathy' as a subtle, early sign of chronic rejection.

sections.title: Recent Advances
sections.content: Recent landmark studies highlight the role of rho-kinase (ROCK) inhibitors (e.g., Netarsudil 0.02%) in promoting endothelial cell survival and migration post-DMEK. Additionally, emerging evidence suggests that topical immunomodulators (Cyclosporine 0.05% or Tacrolimus 0.03%) significantly decrease late endothelial rejection rates in redo settings. The integration of intraoperative digital overlays for graft trephination has improved the precision of button sizing, reducing post-operative astigmatism in complex cases.
